results.summary: The flake was not the clock or the timezone. `tokenExpiryNotice` read `process.env.GITHUB_ACTIONS` itself, so on a runner it wrote the Actions annotation to stdout instead of calling `log` — and the test asserted on `log`. Reproduces with `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true node --test test/doctor.test.js`, no clock involved. Fix: `tokenExpiryNotice(ctx, log, { now, inActions, out })`, defaulted the way `emitAnnotations`/`actionsAnnotation` already default them; tests inject all three so a test picks the branch it means to check and nothing reaches the real stdout. One new test sets GITHUB_ACTIONS=true deliberately and asserts the argument wins — that is the regression guard. The suspected timezone hole is closed anyway: window boundaries walked from both sides (7d+1h ok, 7d ok, 6d23h warn, 1ms warn, 0 expired) at four explicit instants including 02:30Z, 23:30Z and the US spring-forward hour; every case that renders or stamps a date replayed across UTC, America/New_York, Asia/Kolkata and Pacific/Kiritimati; GitHub’s non-ISO header format asserted per zone since it goes through the engine fallback parser. `.github/workflows/test.yml` now runs `npm test` under TZ=UTC and TZ=America/New_York as two steps in one job (same signal, half the runners). Heads-up for whoever picks it up: `tokenExpiryNotice` is exported and tested but nothing imports it — `src/dispatch.js` never calls it, so the loop does not actually warn before KB_TOKEN lapses. Out of scope for #48; worth a card. PR #49.
